sheet-61-1.description: The western half of the sheet shows the north side of Grassy Sound, a resort and fishing settlement on the salt marsh about four miles north of Wildwood, where the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the sound on its way to Anglesea. The railroad runs straight across the part from west to east; the drawing is turned so that north points to the upper left. All the buildings stand in a single row along the west shore of the sound, which runs up and down the sheet at right angles to the railroad, and the map notes that all of them are built on piles over salt marsh covered with water at high tide. A plank walk, lettered Walk, runs behind the row on both sides of the railroad and connects every building by short branch walks. The buildings are small one, one-and-a-half and two storey frame dwellings and cottages, several with names: The Burlington and The Klein north of the track, and to the south Alva, the Lyons Fishing Club, Maguire's, Beers Cottage, Beatrice, Urbane and Idell Cottage, with a house boat moored behind the row. At the south end the walk turns towards a few more cottages where a creek enters the sound. The rest of the part is open marsh, lettered Salt Marsh, and the open water of Grassy Sound to the east. A note beside the railroad says the south side of the sound is about 300 feet away and is shown on the same sheet. The heavy vertical line at the right edge separates this part from the south side.
notes: The plank walk survives as the Boardwalk of the Grassy Sound houses beside Old North Wildwood Boulevard West; the modern lots along it match the drawn row of buildings.
W. J. & S. R. R. is the abandoned Wildwood Branch in OpenStreetMap; North Wildwood Boulevard (NJ 147) now crosses the sound just south of the old line.
Placed from the walk and the railroad line only (no street junctions): one measured point and two points whose position along a line is derived from the scale bar.

Single sheet (N.J.C.M. vol. 4, sheet 61), 100 ft to an inch (scale bar 3.967 px/ft), turned with north about 27 degrees anticlockwise of up. Two parts split by a heavy vertical line: part 1 the north (west) shore of Grassy Sound, a row of cottages on piles along a plank walk either side of the W. J. & S. R. R.; part 2 the south (east) shore with Grassy Sound R. R. Station and Grassy Sound Hotel. No street junctions; both placed by hand from the abandoned Wildwood Branch (OpenStreetMap) and, for part 1, the modern Boardwalk, which follows the drawn walk. Part 2 position along the railroad is uncertain: the sheet says about 300 ft across the sound, the modern parcel shore is about 590 ft; placed on the parcel shore.

sheet-61-2.description: The eastern half of the sheet shows the south side of Grassy Sound, the station end of the small resort settlement where the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the sound between the mainland and Anglesea, about four miles north of Wildwood. The railroad crosses the lower middle of the part from west to east, with platforms on both sides and the Grassy Sound R. R. Station on the south side of the track. North of the track stand the Grassy Sound Hotel, a two storey building beside a platform, a fish house on a pier and a small inlet with walks out over the water; south of the track are a second hotel and two dwellings along the shore. From the station a plank walk, lettered Walk, runs north-east behind a row of cottages and club houses built on piles along the east shore of the sound: the Jas. B. Getz Fishing Club, Charter Oak, the Primrose Rod and Gun Club, Ideal Cottage and a boat house, among several unnamed one and two storey dwellings, each joined to the walk by a short branch. The walk continues off the top edge of the sheet. Everything east of the row is open marsh, lettered Salt Marsh and noted as covered with water at high tide, and a note says all buildings are built on piles. The open water of Grassy Sound fills the west side of the part, with a note that the north side is about 300 feet away and shown on the same sheet. The compass rose straddles the dividing line at the lower left.
notes: Position along the railroad is uncertain: the sheet says the sound is about 300 ft across, but the modern parcel shore on this side lies about 590 ft from the north side; the part is placed on the parcel shore and may be up to about 90 m too far east.
W. J. & S. R. R. is the abandoned Wildwood Branch; OpenStreetMap has no trace of the line east of the sound, so the rail line is extended straight from the north side.
Placed by a two-point helmert (one derived shore point, one point stepped along the railroad at the scale bar's scale): low confidence.
